(more information will follow). fr. crowley november mass for the deceased of the parish: st. mary’s drumagarner on friday 6th november at 7.30pm. the names of the deceased of our parish will be displayed during the month of november. a warm welcome to fr james devine. we are delighted to extend a very warm welcome to fr james devine, who has been appointed to serve in kilrea & desertohill, errigal and granaghan. note from fr. james - thank you all for welcoming me to the parishes this weekend. my name is fr james devine, and i grew up in the waterside area of derry. i was ordained to the priesthood on the 8th december 2013, in st columba's church, long tower, derry. i have four siblings: three older brothers and one younger sister. as a priest, i have served in the parishes of limavady and holy family, ballymagroarty, with a three-year stint in the usa with the marian fathers of the immaculate conception between these two appointments. my most recent appointment has been in the parish of greencastle, co. tyrone, where i had three very happy and fruitful years. i look forward to joining you all in the parishes of granaghan, kilrea and desertoghill, and errigal, and pray that i can be a faithful priest for you, along with fr crowley. we wish fr james every blessing as he begins his ministry among us. let us keep him in our prayers and give him our wholehearted support, not only through our words of welcome, but through our presence, our encouragement and our active participation in the life and mission of the parishes in this area in which he will serve. fr. crowley. plenary indulgence: is applicable from the 1st to the 8th november, for the faithful who visit a cemetery and pray for the deceased and the holy souls. bereavement support group: meeting on thursday 5th november in the marian hall from 7pm - 8.30pm. sharing music, poetry, and reflections. contact moira -

parishes of glendermott & strathfoyle sunday 25th october 2026 thirtieth sunday in ordinary time the commandment of love is the greatest of the commandments, the mother of all the virtues, and the pulsating heart of the christian message. we are created in the image of a god who is love; so, we cannot live without love in today’s gospel reading from matthew, one of the pharisees, a lawyer, asks jesus to identify ‘the greatest commandment of the law’(mt 22:36). in response, jesus quotes the great ‘shema’ prayer recited daily by all devout jews (cf. deut 6:4-5). this prayer exhorts us to love god with our whole heart, mind and soul. jesus immediately adds a second commandment, familiar to his audience namely, ‘love your neighbour as yourself’ (mt 22:39). sadly, the word ‘love’ is so overused in our world today that it has lost much of its meaning. we speak of love of country, love of sport, love of food, love between friends, love of parents, romantic love, etc as pope leo teaches, ‘true love is not merely a fleeting, briefly inflamed emotion. it is more. it is a deep commitment to the other, a decision, a journey and a covenant for life all genuine love is manifested in action; it is practical and outgoing. in the words of st augustine: ‘it has the hands to help others. it has the feet to hasten to the poor and needy. it has the eyes to see misery and want. it has the ears to hear the sighs and sorrows of people.’ such love is demanding. it summons us to leave our comfort zones, to give our time, our energy, our talents, and, indeed, our very selves to others feast of all saints mass arrangements for the feast of all saints- saturday 31st october 6:00pm church of immaculate conception 6:00pm st. oliver plunkett 6:30pm st. columb’s church (note change of time) waterside strathfoyle amalgamated)
